data.narrative:
Gambit is a Seed-stage defense & security company founded by Josh Giegel, Ben Richardson, and Andrew Kemendo, having raised $6.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 10 private and 2 public peers in the Defense & Security sector, including comparable-stage companies like UFORCE, Singularity, and NODA AI.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $6.5M raised as a base proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage advancement, implies a valuation of $16M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (UFORCE at $1.0B, Singularity at $400M, NODA AI at $125M) yields a median valuation of $400M, with a range spanning $125M to $1.0B.

The triangulated analysis across both methods produces a range of $14M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $208M. The substantial gap between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects the inherent tension between Gambit's early capital deployment and the valuation multiples commanded by comparable Defense & Security ventures. Key uncertainties include the relevance of the peer set given Gambit's specific technical positioning, the company's growth trajectory post-Seed, and whether defense sector tailwinds justify median peer multiples for an early-stage entrant. Additional disclosure of Gambit's revenue, customer traction, or technical milestones would narrow this range materially.
